footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $17.2M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 34.7% to $1.3B in 2025. Net interest income rose 14.1% to $1.0B and noninterest income rose 7.3× to $227M; noninterest expense rose 1.3%, and the provision for credit losses was $55.0M, versus $67.0M.
Net income to common rose 5.2× to $313M, or $6.79 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 61.2% versus 81.3%. Texas Capital returned $186M through buybacks.
highlights: Net income to common rose 5.2× to $313M.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
sources: Texas Capital Bancshares, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
